description:
Stage is one service in one environment: which version it runs and how new
versions reach it.

apiVersion.description:
APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object.
Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and
may reject unrecognized values.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#resources

kind.description:
Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents.
Servers may infer this from the endpoint the client submits requests to.
Cannot be updated.
In CamelCase.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds

spec.description:
Spec is one service in one environment. Its environment must be a DNS
label when the Stage is created and is fixed afterwards; a Stage created
before that rule keeps its environment. The rules sit on the Stage, never
on StageSpec, which an Operation's status.policy also copies.

applyRef.description:
ApplyRef is the object the promoter points at a version: a Flux
OCIRepository (it sets spec.ref.digest) or an Argo CD Application (it
sets spec.source.targetRevision). Nothing else is ever written on it.

kind.description:
Kind is OCIRepository (Flux, the default), Application (Argo CD, with
an OCI source and automated sync) or HelmRelease (Flux: the promoter
writes the chart digest on the OCIRepository its spec.chartRef names).

approval.description: ApprovalPolicy can only raise the approval floor, never lower it.

always.description: Always holds every promote for a human, whatever the contracts say.

autonomy.description: AutonomyPolicy tunes when Pacto proposes the next level.

proposeAfter.description: ProposeAfter is how many qualifying promotions earn a proposal.

candidates.description:
Candidates says where new versions come from. At most one of registry,
ociRepositoryRef, upstreamStage and upstreamRecords is set, so the version
offered and the version judged come from the same source; a Stage that sets
none is not Ready and never promotes.

ociRepositoryRef.description:
OCIRepositoryRef is a Flux OCIRepository the promoter only reads: the
candidate is the @sha256: part of its status.artifact.revision.

registry.description:
Registry is the promoter's own registry watch: a new version tag is
a candidate once its Sigstore signature comes from a publisher the
promoter's publisher rule accepts (delivery.publishers).

repository.description:
Repository (host/path) is the repository watched; empty watches the
repository the Stage's applier takes versions from.

upstreamRecords.description:
UpstreamRecords offers what a Stage in another cluster verified, read
from its signed records: the promoter must trust the key that signs
that stream (promoter.upstreamTrust), or it offers nothing.

repository.description: Repository (host/path) is the upstream recorder's streams repository.

stream.description:
Stream is the upstream Stage's stream id, <clusterID>/<namespace>/<name>:
its status.stream.id.

upstreamStage.description: UpstreamStage offers that Stage's verified digests minus its failed ones.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: set at most one of candidates.registry, candidates.ociRepositoryRef, candidates.upstreamStage and candidates.upstreamRecords

deadlines.description: Deadlines override the operation type's defaults (Go durations).

environment.description:
Environment is the environment the Stage delivers to, such as prod.
A promote matches it against the environments the version's contract
declares (environments[].name): a contract that declares environments
must declare this one, with values that satisfy its configuration
schemas, or the promote waits for a person (pacto.environment). It
also places the Pactos and Stages a change's consumers run on, and
selects the values the applier may apply: values-<environment>.yaml or
overlays/<environment>. It is fixed at creation.

gates.description:
Gates configures the Stage's gates. The pre-gates are fixed by the operation
type; the Pacto contract check always verifies, beside the Stage's checks.

declaredConsumersOnly.description:
DeclaredConsumersOnly says every consumer of the service has a
contract Pacto can see, so a breaking change no Pacto depends on ships
without a person. Off by default: a service with no contract can still call it, so
a breaking change with no consumer in sight waits for a person to accept
the unknown.

verify.description: VerifyGates configures what runs after a version is applied.

checks.description:
Checks are this Stage's own verify gates, run beside the Pacto contract
check: a health provider set in delivery.gates.providers, or the built-in
pacto.runtime claim gate.

items.description: GateCheck is one verify gate a Stage runs.

name.description: Name is the gate id its verdicts carry, unique on the Stage.

params.description: Params are the provider's settings (thresholds, filters).

provider.description:
Provider is a gate provider set in delivery.gates.providers, or
pacto.runtime. A Stage cannot name a URL: providers are operator
configuration.

requireObservedModel.description:
RequireObservedModel makes an eval check Unknown unless its runner
says which model answered (observedModel) and the contract declares
an external dependency with a version to compare it with. A model the
runner names that no such version matches fails the check either way.

suite.description:
Suite names a check the version's contract ships (its checks[].name)
for an eval provider to run; without it the provider runs the only check
the version ships. A version whose contract ships no check of that name,
or with no suite ships none or more than one, is held for a person
before it ships.

suiteDigest.description:
SuiteDigest pins the suite's bytes ("sha256:" and 64 hex digits). A
version whose suite has another digest changed its own exam: it is held
for a person before it ships, and an eval check of it is Unknown.

recheck.description:
Recheck is how often the verify gates run again on the version the
Stage runs once it shipped (a Go duration, default 1m). A confirmed Fail
rolls it back; Unknown never does.

window.description:
Window is how long the verify gates may stay Unknown before the
operation is held for a human (a Go duration, default 5m). Re-checks
after release judge the same length of time.

records.description:
RecordsPolicy says whether automation may move the Stage while its records
cannot be written.

required.description:
Required holds every promote or rollback an agent or the promoter
raises for a person to approve while the recorder is not writing this
Stage's records (RecordStoreReady is not True) or more than five of
its operations wait for a record (MaxRecordsPending).

service.description:
ServiceRef is the Pacto ServiceID a Stage delivers: the domain-qualified
service name its contracts declare.

domain.description: Domain is the registry and organisation scope (empty for the default).

startLevel.description:
StartLevel is where a new Stage begins. It is read once, when
status.level is empty; after that only an autonomy operation moves the
level. Creating a Stage is an admin action, so any level is accepted, and
a Stage whose status is lost seeds back to this level. Only observe and
advise keep Pacto from shipping without a person.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: startLevel is fixed at creation; propose delivery.pacto.trianalab.io/autonomy to change the level

workload.description:
Workload is the workload the service runs as, in the Stage's namespace:
the one object pacto.contract and pacto.runtime may judge. The Pacto
resource ships inside every version and names its own target, so
without this a version could point its own check at a decoy. Empty is
the Deployment named spec.service.name.

kind.description: Kind is the workload kind, such as Deployment or StatefulSet.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: environment must be a DNS label, such as production
environment is fixed at creation; create a new Stage

status.description:
StageStatus is written by the promoter's operation and stage reconcilers and
by the recorder (Stream.Head, Stream.Anchor, Stream.RegistryMode and
RecordStoreReady), each through a compare-and-swap on the Stage's
resourceVersion.

applier.description:
Applier is who manages the workloads the Stage delivers, against
spec.applyRef. Written by the promoter's stage reconciler; observed.
since is when this result was first seen, asOf the last observation.

display.description: Display is the one line every surface prints for the manager.

evidence.description: Evidence is what on the workload names the manager.

manager.description:
Manager is the detected manager. Both Flux kinds read flux; Owner names
the kind.

owner.description:
Owner is the object that manages the workloads ("Application
payments/payments").

since.description: Since is when this result was first seen (RFC 3339).

staleAt.description:
StaleAt is when asOf turns stale (RFC 3339): twice the promoter's
resync after asOf, since it rewrites asOf at least once per resync.

values.description:
Values is the values file or Kustomize overlay the applier selects, as
observed on the applyRef object.

workloads.description: Workloads are the workloads checked ("Deployment payments").

authFreshness.description:
AuthFreshness is how old a login the promoter accepts on an approval
(a Go duration). Clients ask for a fresh login with a margin under it
(DecisionFreshnessFor). Empty: no login is too old, and a person
decides with the session they have.

autoHold.description:
AutoHold stops auto-promotion after a person or agent rolled back or
promoted back to a version the Stage already verified.

candidate.description: Candidate is the newest eligible candidate the stage reconciler saw.

conditions.description:
Conditions holds Ready. It is False, naming what is missing, when the
Stage cannot promote: its applier cannot be read, lacks the apply-ref
label or (on Argo CD) has no single OCI source or no automated sync; its
candidate OCIRepository does not exist or sets no spec.verify naming the
publisher; its watched registry cannot be listed or the promoter has no
publisher check; the records of its upstream in another cluster are not
trusted or cannot be read; or it names no candidate source at all. The
recorder adds RecordStoreReady: False when the registry cannot be
reached or holds a stream it refuses to fork; a registry without the
Referrers API never sets it, its records are written as write-once
tags.

items.description:
Condition is a Kubernetes status condition, so `kubectl wait
--for=condition=Ready`, kstatus and Argo CD read it. Write it with
SetCondition.

lastTransitionTime.description: LastTransitionTime is when Status last changed (RFC 3339).

observedGeneration.description: ObservedGeneration is the Stage generation the condition was set from.

failedDigests.description:
FailedDigests are the last 50 versions that failed here; none of them is
promoted again. An older failure drops out.

lastCheck.description: LastCheck is the newest re-check of the running version after it shipped.

at.description: At is when the gates ran (RFC 3339).

operation.description: Operation is the uid of the operation that shipped the version.

items.description: Verdict is one gate's answer plus a citation that can be re-run.

lastOp.description: LastOp is the uid of the operation that last moved the pointer.

level.description:
Level is the Stage's autonomy level. The stage reconciler seeds it from
spec.startLevel; after that only an autonomy operation writes it.

locks.description: Locks maps a facet to the uid of the operation holding it.

observedGeneration.description:
ObservedGeneration is the Stage generation the stage reconciler last
judged Ready from.

observedRevision.description: ObservedRevision is what GitOps' source reports while the Stage observes.

offered.description:
Offered holds the digests a promote carried through pacto.published
with a pass (not an accepted unknown) and that then verified here,
oldest first (cap 50). Only these are offered to a downstream Stage.

pointer.description:
Pointer is the digest the Stage moved the environment to. It is set
when an operation holding the pointer lock starts to apply, before
Flux or Argo CD runs it: Applied on that operation says when they did.

proposal.description: Proposal is the next level Pacto proposes, or why not yet.

items.description: Blocker is one reason the next level is not proposed.

kind.description:
Kind is missing-contract, undeclared-range, unlabelled-apply-ref,
no-observed-digest, no-record-store, needs-verified,
needs-cleared-breaking, incident or partial-graph.

subject.description: Subject is the service, consumer or caller identity.

evidence.description: Evidence names the digests or operation uids that earned it.

level.description: Level is empty while nothing is proposed.

published.description:
Published holds the candidate digests whose signature was verified,
oldest first (cap 50): by Flux on the candidate OCIRepository
(spec.verify naming the publisher's identity), or by the promoter's
registry watch against its publisher rule (candidates.registry). Only
these are promoted from either source.

publisher.description:
Publisher is what the registry watch (candidates.registry) judged:
the rule it judged against and its newest verdicts. Written by the
promoter only.

rule.description:
PublisherRule names the CI identities that may publish. Subject and
Repository are anchored regular expressions, both required; Ref, when set,
must equal the certificate's; Services are path.Match patterns over service
names, and empty means every service.

source.description:
Source is what the watch judges against: the installation's rule, the
signed policy, or none when there is no rule and only a person's pin
accepts a signer.

verdicts.description: Verdicts are the newest judged digests, newest first (cap 20).

items.description: PublisherVerdict is what a publisher check concluded about one digest.

identity.description:
PublisherIdentity is who signed a digest, read from the verified Sigstore
certificate.

class.description:
ActorClass is who raised an operation, as the promoter classifies the
apiserver identity. It is derived, never asserted by the client.

rolledBack.description:
RolledBack holds the uids of the failed operations the promoter raised
its one automatic rollback for, oldest first (cap 50). A failure listed
here never gets a second one.

shadow.description:
Shadow holds the newest would-have decisions while the Stage observes,
newest first.

items.description:
Shadow is what Pacto would have decided for a candidate on a fully
automatic Stage while this one observes, and what then happened. It is
advisory status, never a record.

decision.description: Decision is the floor's decision: approve or accept-unknown.

observedAt.description:
ObservedAt is when GitOps' source reported this candidate (RFC 3339):
not proof of rollout.

plannedAt.description: PlannedAt is when Pacto planned it (RFC 3339).

predicted.description: Prediction is what plan() expects the promoter to do.

verification.description: Verification is the shadow verify on the observed digest.

stream.description: Stream numbers a Stage's concluded operations.

anchor.description:
Anchor is where the stream's records are listed:
<repository>@<anchor digest>. Only the recorder writes it.

approvals.description:
Approvals is where a person's client pushes a signed approval for
this Stage: <approvals repository>@<anchor digest>. Only the
recorder writes it, once.

concluded.description:
Concluded are the newest operations given a seq, each with how it
concluded, written in the compare-and-swap that took the seq. An
operation whose own status write then failed concludes again from
here: the same seq and outcome, never a second seq.

items.description: Concluded is one operation's seq and conclusion, as the Stage holds it.

cause.description:
Cause is the uid of the operation whose failure made the promoter
raise this one: an automatic rollback, freeze or step-down.

clearedBreaking.description:
ClearedBreaking is a promote of a change that is not NON_BREAKING whose
impact verdict passed: every consumer accepts it.

outcome.description: Outcome is how a concluded operation ended.

person.description:
Person is true when the operation carried an approval or a person
raised it.

head.description:
Head is the digest of the newest record in the stream. Only the
recorder writes it.

id.description:
ID is <clusterID>/<namespace>/<name>; the cluster id is the kube-system
namespace uid.

recordedSeq.description:
RecordedSeq is the newest local seq the recorder wrote or adopted a
record for. Only the recorder writes it.

registryMode.description:
RegistryMode is how the recorder writes this stream's records: native
OCI referrers, or one write-once tag per record in the streams
repository when the registry serves no Referrers API. Only the
recorder writes it.

upstreamAcknowledged.description:
UpstreamAcknowledged holds the ids of the unrecordable stand-ins in the
upstream stream that a person on this Stage checked and acknowledged,
oldest first (cap 50). They no longer stop the Stage offering.

upstreamSeen.description:
UpstreamSeen is the newest record this Stage read from the upstream
stream it follows (candidates.upstreamRecords). A later read that ends
before it, or holds another record at its seq, offers nothing, so
records removed from the upstream's tail never go unseen.

record.description: Record is the record's id, the digest of its signed payload.

verified.description: Verified holds the newest verified digests, oldest first (cap 10).
